description: Actual local Lost Link API experiment, 2026-11-04. Full source in the companion ZIP.

plan.title: Lost Link HW7: retrieval coverage and abstention
plan.claim: On campus lost-item queries, alias normalization improves top-3 target retrieval over exact-category plus keyword overlap; test whether this benefit survives absent items and missing category evidence.
plan.primary_check: If answer is present, success means its independently labeled found ID is in the API's top 3; if answer is null, success requires zero candidates. A suggestion is not an ownership decision.
plan.controls: Identical API, database, credentials, public fields, query IDs, k=3, and hardware for every arm. Change only the ranker. Never pass answer labels or private_detail to rankers.
arms: baseline: existing exact category plus raw keyword overlap
original: immutable copy of the repository alias ranker
revised: one evidence-motivated change, frozen before fresh execution
plan.selection: Ten existing paraphrased queries are a legacy regression set, not new held-out evidence. Four new tuning cases vary category evidence and missing fields. Twelve separately saved fresh cases check generalization after the change; synthetic and authored by the same evaluator, not independent human validation.
plan.repetitions: Three timing repetitions, rotating arm order. Rankers are deterministic; repeated rows are not independent accuracy samples. Every query gets one report registration and one search per arm/repetition. Setup is excluded from search latency.
plan.boundary_probe: Unsupported categories and missing type evidence may receive neutral half-credit and return unrelated objects. Include one fresh positive with an unsupported category to measure a conservative gate's recall cost.
plan.client: Two deterministic authenticated API clients (holder registers found items; owner registers lost items and searches). In-process FastAPI TestClient/ASGI, real SQLite and auth/audit middleware. No LLM, external API, human approval, or physical return is measured.
plan.budget: 21 found reports, 26 unique query cases, 3 arms, 3 timing repetitions; no paid model calls. Bounded local synthetic data only.
plan.freeze_rule: Run discovery on tuning only, inspect failures, change once, hash the revised source and fresh fixture before running fresh cases, then make no result-driven tuning.
plan.interpretation: Report negative results and unsupported categories. No claims about real users, autonomous LLM planning, ownership verification accuracy, network latency, throughput, or production readiness.

change.observed: Original alias ranker suggested candidates for all 3 absent-item tuning cases T01-T03; baseline abstained on all 3. Both retrieved the target for T04, whose type appears only in its description.
change.cause: Unknown type earns 0.20 category credit. With unknown colour/location/date the total reaches MIN_SCORE=0.45 even with no shared words. Metadata matches can raise unrelated items still further.
change.one_change: Require a non-null normalized query category and the same normalized category in each candidate before applying the unchanged score and threshold. No aliases, weights, thresholds, or baseline rules changed.
change.expected_cost: Abstention also suppresses real items of an unsupported category. H06 is a pre-saved fresh positive watch case designed to expose this tradeoff, not to tune the policy.
change.fresh_rule: Freeze source and fixture hashes in retest_manifest before any fresh API request; report every fresh case without changing the rule. Legacy queries are regression checks. T01-T04 are tuning, never held-out.

manifest.transport: in-process ASGI, SQLite, real auth/audit middleware
manifest.id_generation: deterministic sequential IDs for reproducible rank tie ordering
manifest.tokens: ephemeral synthetic local fixture tokens; never exported
manifest.latency_scope: one GET including ASGI/auth/SQLite/audit; excludes seed, registration, model and network
